Senses.Explanation: Marvelous function names effective or responsive activity contrasted with, or joined to, an underlying body or source. Shengyin Zi permits free marvelous functioning after the locked barrier is broken through. Linji Yixuan asks whether an impossible feat is marvelous function or merely how things naturally are; Tianyi Yihuai says usual powers and eloquence fail in the raised crisis. Yongming Yanshou pairs constant body with marvelous function, Huineng says its instances are innumerable, and Zhuanyu Guanheng warns that powers called marvelous do not remove attachment.

Senses.Explanation: To appraise and distinguish is to test, sort, or discriminate people, responses, or stated teaching positions. To appraise, sort out, or distinguish; noun constructions name the resulting appraisal or classificatory distinction. The term is attested 266 times in 126 texts. Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu's unnamed questioner sets two episodes side by side and asks Nanyue to “please appraise and distinguish” them (兩段不同，試請料揀); Wuyi Yuanlai asks who can sort out a presented conjunction. The same appraisal vocabulary appears in Linji's “Four Selections” (四料揀). The Eye of Humans and Gods records Nanyuan Huiyong asking Fengxue Yanzhao, “the Four Selections—what do the selections select?” (四料揀，料揀何法), and compiler Huiyan Zhizhao begins another exposition with people of middle and lower capacity under that heading. Zhanran Yuancheng calls paired evaluative formulas “the old so-called selection sayings” (古所謂料揀語). The public act, resulting distinction, and named set remain one appraisal-and-selection family; noun and verb grammar alone do not create different lexical things.

Senses.Explanation: Panning gold from sand is discriminating the sought gold from surrounding grit. Xueguan Zhiyin makes that separation a verdict on a public case, while Dulang says someone who sees before the formal address need not pan at all. After raising Nanquan's exchange with Yangshan over selecting vegetables, Xueguan Zhiyin says that picking weeds from a waste field still leaves grass, whereas panning sand for gold recognizes gold. His verse then insists that marrow, skin, and hair be distinguished. Wanru Tongwei says deep labor obtains gold from sand, then contrasts that work with seeking the Way in written words: clarity comes only when verbal explanation is left behind. Huijue Yi calls panning gold easy beside producing a lotus in fire while addressing a lay patron. Dulang turns the image around. If the assembly understands before he ascends the seat, it will not pan gold from sand; if not, the community must join in the monastery's construction. Across these cases the image names discriminating work, but a timely meeting can make that work unnecessary.

Senses.Explanation: A renunciant monastic is a person who has left household life and entered the monastic order. Weilin Daopei raises a definition attributed to Shakyamuni that links the name with leaving one's family, recognizing mind, reaching the source, and understanding what is unconditioned. Baizhang Huaihai treats a monastic as an already ordained audience requiring different instruction from a layperson, and elsewhere calls ritual conduct and the four immeasurables the monastic's proper work while forbidding attachment to them. Senses.Explanation: Zhaozhou's 'drink tea' is the compact case-name for Zhaozhou Congshen sending both the newcomer and the previously arrived person to drink tea, then giving the same instruction to the monastery officer who objects; later masters raise that even-handed serving as a difficult piece of house business rather than ordinary hospitality. Ying'an Tanhua says he fears Zhaozhou's tea because its recipient is either a creditor or an enemy, making the offered cup a charged encounter rather than refreshment. Zuliang Qi repeats Ying'an's warning after his own assembly fails to answer the raised case, then says he does not fear the tea and asks how a patch-robed monk would be handled. Yuanwu Keqin lists Zhaozhou's tea beside Linji's sword, Deshan's final phrase, Juzhi's finger, and Heshan's drum as house devices whose point is one when directly confirmed. Lianfeng Su mocks reducing it to wet lips, while Xiangya Ting ranks it among famous devices that still do not receive his approval as the matter beyond. The corpus therefore keeps the case alive by praise, fear, comparison, and criticism.

Senses.Explanation: A great elephant pictured entering a river, cutting through the current, and reaching the bottom. 'Fragrant elephant' is the conventional graph-by-graph rendering, but the stored headword passages do not describe an odor; they make the animal visible through size, force, river crossing, current, and depth. The dominant Chan family is 'the fragrant elephant fords the river' (香象渡河), attested 65 times in 49 texts and repeatedly completed by 'cuts through the current and passes' (截流而過) or 'cuts through the current to the bottom' (截流到底). Yuejiang Zhengyin sets the crossing beside the white ox in a snow address. Gumei Dinglie compares breaking a barrier and changing course to the elephant cutting through the current, paired with the golden-winged bird splitting the sea. An unnamed Chan visitor asks Xiangtian Jinian for 'the matter of getting to the bottom' in the river-crossing line; Xiangtian answers with a great whale drinking the western river and exposing coral. Shending Yikui calls it a current-cutting dynamic; Wuyi Yuanlai compares an unobstructed person to the crossing; Caoshan Benji turns hearing the crossing into a public question; and Yuanwu Keqin says even unobstructed current-cutting has not yet earned the inherited matter. These are named uses of one forceful animal scene in addresses, questions, appraisals, and comparisons, not evidence that the elephant itself names one abstract referent.
